notes: Shared session STANDARDS for all Training Arcade campaigns — how FIT and FIGHT sessions are prescribed, counted, voiced, and (for weights) set up. Applies across every campaign's modules. Spec: specs/27-arcade-session-standards.md. This file is the single source of truth for the volume ladder, the weighted-workout builder flow, the announcer scripts, and the fight-round rules. VALUES MARKED 'proposed' ARE PENDING SIGN-OFF (some are placeholders for the app team to tune + test).

fit_prescription.rule: EVERY bodyweight exercise in a FIT module carries an explicit prescription: sets, reps, and a count_mode — no more un-quantified 'do push-ups'. Reps are COUNTED so the user can follow along (voice + on-screen counter).

exercise_shape.name: string — the movement
exercise_shape.category: pull | push | squat_legs | core | explosive | hold | carry
exercise_shape.reps: int — per set (for hold/carry use seconds via 'duration_sec' instead)
exercise_shape.duration_sec: int — for holds/carries instead of reps
exercise_shape.count_mode: reps | cadence | time | none — how the voice counts it (default reps)

fit_prescription.count_toggle: Rep counting (voice) is ON by default and follows every counted set; it is suppressed when the announcer/voice is toggled OFF (see voice-guidance). On-screen counter still runs.
fit_prescription.pull_up_note: Pull/muscle-up movements scale on their OWN lower curve (you can't rep 50 pull-ups) — see volume_ladder.by_category.pull.

volume_ladder.rule: Reps/sets START basic and climb PER STAGE. Volume scales by (a) the campaign's stage TIER and (b) the movement CATEGORY (a pull-up ≠ a squat) and (c) difficulty (easy/normal/hard). These are PROPOSED, safety-passed numbers — the user's brainstorm ('1 set of 250', '10 sets of 20') is interpreted as high-volume EASY movements only, capped; hard/loaded movements stay in sane ranges.
volume_ladder.status: confirmed — CALIBRATED with the user as the elite HARD/peak ceiling, the average person mapped down to easy/normal. Explicit sets x reps per difficulty per tier (no multiplier). Reps are COUNTED.
volume_ladder.calibration_note: User (a strong athlete) reference points used as the HARD-peak ceiling: 5x10 pull-ups easy for them / 5x30 challenging; 5x100 abs; 5x50 squats not-too-hard / 5x100 hard; 4x2min holds challenging. So HARD@peak targets their 'challenging' level; NORMAL and EASY are scaled down for average/committed users. Their most extreme feats (5x100 squats/abs, 4x2min) live in the signature_challenge, not the base ladder.
volume_ladder.format: each cell is { sets, reps } (or { sets, sec } for holds), per difficulty. Peak targets: pull 30+, push 50, squat 50-60, core 50-75, hold 2-3min (all HARD).

pull.note: pull-ups/muscle-ups. HARD peak 5x30 is an ELITE ceiling (user-calibrated) — most users won't reach it; band-assist, negatives, or fewer reps scale it. NEVER hit the number with kipping or partial reps.

core.note: abs tolerate high volume; the user's 5x100 lives in signature_challenge.

hold.note: planks/wall-sits, count_mode 'time'. HARD peak 4x2min = user's 'challenging'; a 3-min hold is the signature finale challenge.

explosive.note: jumps/plyo — total foot-contacts ALWAYS respect the campaign's plyo foot-contact cap; never exceed it to hit a rep number.

signature_challenge.rule: A campaign's finale MAY carry ONE high-volume 'signature' challenge for the anime feel — ONLY on a safe low-skill category (squats, abs, calf raises, holds), spread across sets, difficulty-scaled, never a grinding single set of a hard movement.

abs_hundred.label: Iron Core — up to the user's 5x100

safety_caps.pull_note: 30 is the HARD-peak ceiling only; band-assist / negatives / fewer reps scale it. No kipping or partial reps to reach it.
never: grinding a hard movement (pull/push) for extreme reps
exceeding the plyo cap via jumps
sacrificing form to hit the number

weighted_flow.rule: When a movement needs/allows WEIGHT, the FIT session works partly like Workout Builder + Quick Mission: a review-and-approve setup, then a generated session.

setup_screen.announcer: States the STAGE + TITLE, then 'review your workouts and get ready' — giving the user time to set up.
per_exercise_actions: APPROVE — a check mark confirms the exercise as-is
SWAP — swap for a similar weighted movement (same category/target)
MAKE BODYWEIGHT — convert a weighted movement to a bodyweight equivalent, which RE-RANGES it to a very high rep count equivalent to the weighted work (e.g. weighted row -> high-rep inverted rows)
MAKE WEIGHTED — convert a bodyweight movement to a weighted equivalent (user enters load), which re-ranges it to a lower, heavier rep band
setup_screen.generate_button: Stays inactive until ALL exercises are approved/adjusted; then it ACTIVATES and GLOWS. User taps -> the session is generated.

bodyweight_to_weighted_reranging.rule: Converting bodyweight<->weighted swaps the rep band: bodyweight = high reps (endurance/volume), weighted = lower reps at load. Keep total stimulus roughly equivalent.

weighted_flow.announcer_go_script: On generate + countdown: '3, 2, 1. Stage {n}: {persona/title}. {exerciseCount} workout(s). {exerciseName}, {setIndex} of {setCount} sets, {reps} reps! Ready — go!'  (e.g. 'Stage 5: Jack Hanma. 1 workout, Muscle-ups, 1 of 5 sets, 20 reps! Ready go!')

bodyweight_counted.rule: Bodyweight sets are REP-COUNTED — the voice + counter count each rep so the user follows along. Counting is suppressed only if the announcer/voice is toggled OFF (on-screen counter still shows).
bodyweight_counted.per_set_rounds: Every movement runs SET BY SET — 'Set 1 of 3' -> rest -> 'Set 2 of 3' -> rest -> 'Set 3' — never one long undivided block (Baki playtest fix).

count_pace_by_category.rule: The counting cadence matches the movement: pull-ups count SLOW, squats moderate, push-ups brisk. Weighted movements are timed, never counted.

weighted_timed.rule: For WEIGHTED work, after the announcer says 'go', a TIMER counts how long the round/set takes to complete. The user presses COMPLETE -> a bell rings -> rest begins.

adaptive_rest.rule: Rest length is computed from how long the set took AND the load entered — heavier + longer sets earn more rest. (Formula TBD; see engine placeholder.)

fight_standard.rule: FIGHT sessions are FIGHT-FOCUS rounds (or COMBO-COACH based). Rounds may be NAMED for a franchise specialty, but every strike MUST resolve to one of the 4 canonical disciplines — pick the move equivalent.

franchise_move_equivalents.rule: A franchise-flavored move maps to a real canonical strike. The NAME can be thematic; the executed technique is canonical.

examples.canonical: committed power cross (speed, not max-force chase)

combo_generation.rule: Arcade fight rounds route through the SAME combo generator as Combo Coach / Fight Focus — combos are GENERATED live and called by voice, never hardcoded into campaign data. Each fight round carries a `combo_spec` that seeds the generator.

combo_spec_shape.generate_combos: bool — true: numbered combos generated + voiced (Combo Coach style); false: technique/movement cues called instead (grappling, stance, footwork rounds)
combo_spec_shape.focus: string — the round's seed theme (e.g. hooks_body, jab_cross, chain_punches, counter)
combo_spec_shape.allowed_strikes: string[] — the strike vocabulary the generator may draw from this round
combo_spec_shape.allowed_defense: string[] — optional defensive calls mixed in (slip-left, slip-right, roll)
combo_spec_shape.complexity: single | intro | basic | standard | advanced | burst — base combo length band (engine scales by difficulty)
combo_spec_shape.phantom: bool — shadow-fight an imagined opponent (attack cue -> your response)
combo_spec_shape.technique_cues: string[] — the cue script when generate_combos is false (or mixed rounds)
combo_spec_shape.emphasis: string — one coaching emphasis the voice repeats

strike_vocabulary.note: Same numbering as Combo Coach / Training Camp — one vocabulary app-wide. Kick/knee/elbow tokens only in kickboxing/muay_thai/mma rounds.

complexity_bands.note: combo length (strikes per call); difficulty shifts the max (easy -1, hard +1) via arcade-session-engine resolveComboParams

focus_saturation.rule: A focused round is SATURATED with its focus but never monotonous: ~60% of generated calls draw purely from the round's allowed_strikes; ~40% are MIXED calls that lead with a focus strike then draw from the discipline's wider pool (hooks, uppercuts, body shots — kicks/knees/elbows in kick disciplines) plus occasional head movement (slip/roll). From the Baki playtest: a jab-cross round should still sprinkle a lead hook, an uppercut, a double jab, head movement — here and there, not intensely.
focus_saturation.exempt: complexity 'single' (one-perfect-strike drills, e.g. the karate cross) stays 100% focus; cue-based rounds unchanged

combo_generation.mixed_rounds: A grappling/stance round may set mixed_with_cue: true — it then generates combos from allowed_strikes AND keeps its technique_cues, interleaving two generated calls with one cue. Use it so a fight-only player never runs two consecutive stages without a combo called; the remaining rounds stay honestly cue-based.

finishers.rule: Random explosive BODYWEIGHT finishers may be inserted BETWEEN rounds or at the END as a finisher. Capped, voiced, and (jumps) counted toward the plyo cap.
finishers.dosing: short, capped bursts (e.g. 20-40s or a small rep count); never to failure; jumps count toward the campaign plyo foot-contact cap

fight_standard.guided_and_voiced: All rounds, combinations, and finishers are guided and called out by the voice (voice-guidance contract, specs/22) with the campaign's voice pack.

integrations.voice_guidance: Rep counts, cadence, combination callouts, announcer scripts, and finisher cues all run through the shared audio-guided timer (specs/22).
integrations.workout_builder_and_quick_mission: The weighted setup flow reuses Workout Builder's swap/approve UX and Quick Mission's generate-and-go pattern.
integrations.difficulty_scaling: Volume ladder + rep bands multiply by the campaign's easy/normal/hard difficulty.
integrations.plyo_caps: Explosive reps + jump finishers always respect the campaign's plyo foot-contact cap.
